summary: Most of the video path is generic JTFRAME machinery (vtimer, jtframe_scroll tilemaps, jtframe_objscan/objdraw line-buffer sprites), which says little either way. The board-specific logic leans on MAME. The layer mixer reproduces the nested decision tree of tecmo_mix_device::mix_bitmaps and its palette-offset parameters (regular/blend_comp/blend_source/bgpen), and the protection MCU is a high-level transliteration of MAME's protection_w with MAME's jump tables instead of the board's D8749. A few hardware-flavoured touches exist: scroll offsets done as a subtractor, sprite tile composition done as ROM address-bit substitution, and per-line sprite scanning. But no module follows a board chip or schematic block.

findings.signal: Mixer is MAME's mix_bitmaps decision tree
findings.note: casez on {sprite opaque, ~prio} then the tx > fg > bg opacity chain, with blend pairs (obj over fg/bg/bgpen, fg over bg/bgpen) picked exactly where MAME calls sum_colors. MAME's rand() placeholders are filled with simple choices. ~oprio reproduces set_revspritetile (XOR 3).

findings.signal: Palette offsets and names copy the MAME mixer config
findings.note: OBJ=0,TEXT=1,SCR1=2,SCR2=3 banks with BLEND_COMP=+0x400 and BLEND_SRC=+0x800. SEL_BGPEN gives 0x600 and FILL gives 0x200: exactly MAME's m_*regular_comp, m_*blend_comp, m_*blend_source, m_bgpen and m_bgpen_blend values, and the names follow MAME's member names.

findings.signal: Protection MCU replaced by MAME's HLE state machine
findings.note: Same command-nibble switch (0x0 init, 0x1/0x2 code MSB/LSB returning 0x10/0x20, 0x3-0x6 returning 0x40-0x70|nibble of jumppoint). The board's D8749 MCU is not modelled.

findings.signal: Jump tables identical to MAME's, including the -2 mode switch
findings.note: The 17 wildfang entries and the sparse raiga bootup/gameplay tables match MAME value for value. SWITCH=-2 switches the table the same way MAME's m_protmode does.
Per-channel add with saturation of two palette lookups, matching MAME's min(0xFF, c1+c2). It is plausible hardware, but it is the same abstraction and has no board-specific structure.

findings.signal: Per-game sprite buffering mirrors MAME's live/buffered choice
findings.note: Header-selected NO/SINGLE/DOUBLE frame buffer reproduces MAME's live spriteram for gaiden and its 2-frame lag for raiga, and vsize_en matches MAME's sprite_sizey=2. This is per-game configuration, not board structure.

findings.signal: Sprite tile composition as ROM address-bit substitution
findings.note: MAME masks the tile number and adds layout[row][col]. The HDL instead overrides individual ROM address bits with the h/v sub-tile counters (haddr, vaddr, hadj), the way a counter-driven address generator would.

Sprite RAM is scanned per line with an in-zone test against vrender and a 9-pixel line-buffer output delay (jtgaiden_obj.v:118-132), not drawn as a per-frame batch. Part of this comes from the JTFRAME objscan template, so it is weak evidence.

findings.signal: Scroll offset as a register subtractor, MAME constants absent
findings.note: Y scroll = scroll register minus offset register, built as a latched adder. MAME's set_scrolldy magic constants (0x20, 0x2ff, 0x3b2...) do not appear, and the x-offset registers are ignored.

findings.signal: Address decode, interrupts and ports follow the shared memory map
findings.note: Range comparisons on A[19:12] and register selects on A[9:8]/A[3:1] match the map, as both sides must. IRQ5 is set on VBL and cleared by the 0x7a806 write.
Timing comes from jtframe_vtimer with octal constants, and the tile layers are thin wrappers around jtframe_scroll. Neither names any board net or chip.
